local_thickness — 2D morphology op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "local_thickness", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Returns each foreground pixel filled with "the diameter of the largest circle that can cover it" (local thickness).

b is the threshold above which the bright side counts as foreground (0.1–0.9). a is the upper radius limit measured (1–12 pixels), and the output is divided by that limit to fit in [0,1] —— when you need absolute values, recover the limit from a and multiply back.

A classic quantity that gives particle size, pore size and wall thickness as "a single map"; it is the same as morphological

granulometry: if a pixel has the value r, that pixel survives an opening with a disc of radius r. The implementation is straightforward: the distance transform gives the inscribed-circle radius, and in descending order of radius each circle is written into the area it covers.

Applicability: (1) The foreground is decided by a single threshold, so with uneven illumination the thickness becomes biased by location —— flatten first with local_threshold or similar. (2) Structures thicker than the limit a level off at the limit (whether it saturates shows in the output maximum sticking at 1.0).

(3) It is a pixel-unit quantity, so once the diameter drops below 3 pixels the quantization step exceeds 30%.

Uses: pore-size distribution in casting voids and foams, powder particle size, detection of thin-walled sections, fibre thickness. The 3-D version is vol_wall_thickness in ops3d. HALCON has no corresponding single op.
